sense.text: Satan’s agenda is to cause you men to forget the mission and be distracted; we must not stop teaching and raising up our people because of foolishness, evil speech, gossip and slander. This is John the Revelator, exiled on the island of Patmos in a salt mine, seeing things. When you read the Book of Revelation, understand that the explanation of the visions and similitudes was not given to John; it is given to us now in these last days. “And, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion”: the Lamb represents Christ. John the Baptist said, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. “And with him an hundred forty and four thousand”: there is a doctrine going around that we don’t know definitively who the tribes of Israel are. “Having his Father’s name written in their foreheads”: why? Because they overcame their trials and tribulations.

precepts.why: This shows how the prophets received visions and how they explain things. “I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

“Holding the four winds of the earth”: the four winds represent the militaries of the world. When we step outside the wind is blowing, so this wind is not literal wind; it is representative of destruction. “Nor on the sea”: there are militaries on the sea, navies. “To whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”: that is the proof it is talking about destruction. “Till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads”: we have to be sealed with the laws of God and the testimony. All Israelites say I’m sealed with the law until test time comes; then the Most High separates the men from the boys and the women from the girls. We shall through much tribulation enter into the kingdom. Nobody is sneaking into the kingdom; you got to earn this by righteousness. “There were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”: these are the leaders.

What is the seal of the living God? “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples”: the seal is his testimony and the law. Back in the day, in a video from 1993, I was saying it was the shield of David, and we all walked around with the hexagram; that is not what the seal is talking about.

This goes with Isaiah 8:16 and Revelation 7 regarding the seal in the foreheads. “With the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”: because we were split into two kingdoms. “Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers”: not according to animal sacrifice; that was the old covenant. “And I regarded them not”: he sent us into captivity. “I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts”: that’s the point; that is what being sealed in our foreheads means. Verse 11, “And they shall not teach every man his neighbour,” is clearly talking about the kingdom. People try to say verse 11 is for today; it’s not for today.
The precept for Hebrews 8:11. “And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord”: that goes back to when the scriptures say Christ will deal with us face to face. That’s the kingdom.

This ties in with the numbskulls that say nobody knows who the twelve tribes are or who Judah is. “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”: Judah is going to be the first of the tribes to wake up and get the understanding of who they are. That is why Revelation 7 names Judah first.

What is Judah going to do once they get the knowledge? “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”: Judah is going to teach. “And bring him unto his people”: in order to bring Judah to his people, Judah got to know who his people are: that’s Benjamin over there, that’s Levi, that’s Simeon, that’s Ephraim. His people would be scattered in all nations, and Judah would be the one going to them. “Let his hands be sufficient for him”: Judah is always going to be at a fight against the enemy, particularly Edom. “And be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

Hold Deuteronomy 33:7. “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”: people read that and lose their minds, but the New Testament is not separate from the Old Testament. The two go hand in hand; you just got to put the pieces of the puzzle together.

This uses the word that Matthew 28:19 used. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”: this is a curse upon the twelve tribes. “And ye shall be left few in number”: because they were killing a lot of us. So Judah would have to know these are Israelites here, this is that tribe, this is that tribe; we might not know a tribe yet, but it is coming, and we are going to teach him anyway. That’s what is going on right now.

“Of the tribe of Juda were sealed twelve thousand.” “After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations”: between the sealing and the destruction you have men, women and children coming into this truth. “Clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands.”

“Behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”: that’s the 144,000 of Revelation 7:4. “Which are departed from the shadow of the world”: which is sin. “Take thy number, O Sion”: it is telling you who they are; Sion is another name for Israelites. “Which have fulfilled the law of the Lord”: when you see Israelites not keeping the law, if they cannot apply basic law, love your neighbour as yourself, get away from them. “The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”: Christ said when this gospel shall be preached in all the world, then shall the end come. You think everybody has to hear it; it ain’t talking about that. When the 144,000 is reached, that’s it. When the last one is sealed, then destruction comes.

“I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number”: this is saying the same thing as Revelation 7:9. “And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest”: it calls him a young man because he died in his early thirties, and he is going to come back with that same body. “It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world.” “Them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord”: the name of the Lord refers to his law and his testimony.

Christ is the one that crowns them. “And if a man also strive for masteries”: the mastery we are all striving for is to be part of the elect. “Yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully”: the operative word is lawfully. If you think you are going to slander your way to a crown, or shuck and jive your way to a crown, that ain’t happening with the Most High. How do you know if you are striving lawfully? There are going to be tests from the Lord; test that brother, test that sister, test them as a congregation.

Every week we get an email about a new name of God. “Him that overcometh”: overcomes your own personal sins, your trials in your marriage, your trials amongst the congregation. “Will I make a pillar in the temple of my God”: to be a pillar means a leader. “And he shall go no more out”: not going out into captivity no more. “And I will write upon him the name of my God”: when you overcome. Check YouTube and you’ll see every camp with a different name, and they’ll all condemn you to death if you don’t say it; I used to do it. We are still here in captivity; what are you talking about, you overcame already?

This is why the Israelite camps hate us. Some brothers say Yahawah, some say Ahayah, some say Yahweh; I ain’t arguing with none of y’all. “My determination is to gather the nations”: God says I do want all nations together, to destroy them. “To pour upon them mine indignation.” “For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent”: once he destroys the nations and their militaries, then he will give us the pure language. It is going to be one name and one pronunciation. I’m not the most educated brother in Israel, but I can read basic English; it said then. You got the pure language already? So you bypassed God’s prophecies? Reading is fundamental.

sense.text: “And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters”: many waters means loud. “And I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps”: don’t ask me who the harpers are; that is in heaven, above my pay grade.

“And they sung as it were a new song before the throne”: we went over the song of the Lamb and the song of Moses. “And before the four beasts, and the elders”: don’t ask me who the four beasts or the elders in heaven are either. “And no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand”: these are teachers; these are the ones that can learn the song and take you precept upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little. This is why we tell you men to study. “Which were redeemed from the earth.”

precepts.why: This new song the Christian church don’t sing; you sing this and everybody says you got the devil on you. “And his praise in the congregation of saints”: the next verse proves the saints are Israel, not all races on the planet. “Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: the problem with our people is we have been rejoicing in Esau. You prove who you rejoice in by the holidays you keep. If you celebrate Christmas, Thanksgiving, Easter, New Year’s, Valentine’s Day, even Kwanzaa, you are rejoicing in the devil, because God did not establish them. He established the Sabbath, Passover, the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of weeks, the memorial of blowing of trumpets, the day of atonement, the feast of tabernacles, the feast of dedication; if you ain’t keeping them days, you are rejoicing in the devil. “Let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: we got to acknowledge we do have a king. Eye hath not seen what God hath prepared for them that love him; Thor, Krypton, the elf kingdom in Lord of the Rings, that’s ghetto compared to what he’s setting up here on earth. “Let them praise his name in the dance”: people get mad when we dance; we going to dance. “For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people”: not all nations. “Let the high praises of God be in their mouth”: his laws, the law and the testimony. “And a twoedged sword in their hand; To execute vengeance upon the heathen”: vengeance ain’t words; vengeance is actions. Another word for it is payback, retribution, justice, and we have never seen justice in today’s society. “To bind their kings with chains.” “To execute upon them the judgment written”: we are not going by our own mind; we do exactly what the written judgment says. “This honour have all his saints.” If we bring the right understanding of this scripture out in the media, we will be crucified.

“Which were redeemed from the earth.” “O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee”: who did he redeem? Jacob, Israel, the same people. “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” The ones redeemed from the earth is Israel.

sense.text: “These are they which were not defiled with women”: it don’t mean what you are thinking. The Lord deals with women, everything in his proper order: he dealt with our foremothers Sarah and Rebekah, and with Huldah, who knew the scriptures very well, but they were not setting themselves up as leaders over the men. “For they are virgins”: it does not mean they never had sex; it means undefiled with philosophies and sin. “These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth”: whatever the scriptures say to do, the sheep, the elect, are going to do it, no excuses, no matter how hard. That’s why there must be tests: we all say we love the Lord, and your trial proves whether you love the Lord or not. “These were redeemed from among men”: the 144,000 of men. “Being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.”

precepts.why: “And I find more bitter than death the woman”: let’s see what type of woman. Some brothers bring it out like God hates all women; that is not what he is saying. “Whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands”: this is the type of woman some of you are married to. She don’t want you to do nothing with the scriptures: why you always with the brothers, why you always in the Bible, why you always got to go to camp? I asked a brother one time do you have peace at home with your wife; he said yes, as long as we don’t open the Bible. “Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”: if you want to please the Lord, get away from her.

Being defiled by women is an allegory, a similitude, in terms of philosophies; the first philosophy came through Eve, and we all die. “And sit not in the midst of women.” “For from garments cometh a moth, and from women wickedness”: the Most High knows what he made.

Your two main obstacles in striving to become part of the elect are going to be money and women; every problem we counsel comes back to those two. “Let go from thee mortal thoughts, cast away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature”: it is talking about sin, and you know what you are weak to. “And set aside the thoughts that are most heavy unto thee”: money and women; put them thoughts aside. “And haste thee to flee from these times.”

Read this history on your own: Athaliah set herself up as queen, killing all the sons that were to be set on the throne; Israel hid one son until he could be revealed as king, and Athaliah had an army. “Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword”: they didn’t play. The Most High don’t deal with weak-natured men following women. “For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord.” The scriptures are meant to transform you from one man into another; that is part of why we set up the Men of Valor program.

People say rank is evil; rank is your place in the kingdom. “Which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”: there’s no gate called Negro Baptist or Puerto Rican Catholic; you got to come through one of the gates. “And in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb”: the twelve apostles are part of the 144,000, but they are the top of it.

“Ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel”: that’s rank right there. Christ is going to give the twelve the order, they are going to give the rest of the 144,000 the orders, and we will all obey. There ain’t going to be no confusion.

This shows that being a virgin is not talking about sex, because Peter is the top of the apostles. “But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever”: Simon Peter had a wife. Peter the apostle was married.

The real understanding of being a virgin: “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” A chaste virgin means pure, undefiled; if it ain’t talking about sex, it is talking about philosophies and sin.
“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.” “Wherefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me.”

This is the main one. “He goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice”: Christ is talking about himself. “And a stranger will they not follow”: they are not following strange doctrines and strange philosophies.
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me”: that is what it means to follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth.
“These were redeemed from among men.” “And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men.”

“Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man”: there is a divine order; the Most High deals with men first and foremost. The women that love the Lord are going to fall in line with that; those with the Jezebel spirit are going to be angry and say why aren’t we equal, the white man says we’re equal. That’s not what God says.

What does being the firstfruits mean? We have a high holy day called firstfruits. “That we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures”: when we wake up to this truth we are a kind of firstfruits; not a literal firstfruit like an apple or an orange. That’s how the Lord sees us that come into his truth.

sense.text: “And in their mouth was found no guile”: guile is sly or cunning intelligence: craftiness, artfulness, deviousness, wiles, ploys, schemes, stratagems, manoeuvres, subterfuges, tricks, ruses, deception, deceit, duplicity, underhandedness, double dealing, treachery, fraud. Think about all that we have been going through at IUIC in the past couple of months; it all fits. The elect is not going to have guile in their mouth, and all them videos you see on YouTube can be put in one word: guile. Men who left say they’re still in the truth, but their classes are not edifying anybody; they are all personal attacks, saying the ranking system is evil. Rank has been set up from the beginning; a rank is a title for order’s sake, and your rank is based upon your works. Everything in existence has an order: the sun comes out in the day, the moon at night, the water doesn’t go beyond the shoreline. Rank and order are synonymous; when you are against rank you are against order, and the Bible calls that disorderly. God deals with order: angels, archangels, Christ above all, and the Father; in First Corinthians, God, the Son, man, woman and child. “For they are without fault before the throne of God”: this is what we are trying to attain.

precepts.why: Rank in the Old Testament: “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates.”

For those who say that’s not the New Testament: “That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city”: to ordain an elder means there must be a ranking system. Bishops, deacons and captains are elders. The Mormons ride around on bicycles with Elder on their name tags and nobody has a problem with that, but when our people set up rank and structure, it’s evil.

This is what you men don’t want to be. When we started off it was three families, boots on the ground; we didn’t drag people from old congregations with us. You’re not a teacher of God if you have to steal, trick or beguile people to follow you. “Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them”: if you have to draw away disciples after you, you are not of the elect; you are a deceiver, a traitor, a defector, a derelict, treacherous.
“Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile”: that’s what the Lord is looking for from every man and every woman. Don’t let your mouth speak guile.

“Wherefore laying aside all malice, and all guile”: malice is the intention or desire to do evil: ill will, spite, hostility, hatred, bitterness, vindictiveness, revenge, backbiting, rancour, grudge. “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word.”

This is how all of us must be; we cannot have guile, deceit, trickery or craftiness in our mouth. “Let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile”: these are things we must put in practice. It’s not enough just reading it; when you are tempted to speak evil, close your lips. “But the face of the Lord is against them that do evil”: all you men and women who ran out of here and are speaking evil now, the Lord is against you. That’s not something I wrote; I’m reading the scriptures.

“Without fault before the throne of God.” “Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory”: all this is of the Lord; he presents us faultless.

Paul explains how we can become faultless in this truth. “Who walk not after the flesh”: after guile, deceit, treachery and evil, “but after the Spirit”: the laws of God. That’s how we are found faultless, without condemnation; walk in the spirit.
